html:
The Rus' trade treaty of 907 is an agreement between Byzantium and the Rus' recorded in the Primary Chronicle of Kiev. It is said to have followed a raid on Constantinople by Prince Oleg, who ruled from Kiev.

The chronicle tells that Oleg's ships came to the walls, and that the emperors Leo VI and his brother Alexander paid a large tribute and granted terms. Rus' merchants could come to the city, stay in the suburb of St Mamas and receive food, baths and ship's gear, but had to enter unarmed, in groups of no more than fifty, and leave before winter.

No Byzantine source mentions the raid, and historians doubt parts of the story. The fuller treaty of 911, whose text the chronicle gives with a list of envoys with Norse names, is more widely accepted. Both show the weight of the Dnieper route, the road from the Varangians to the Greeks, which carried furs, wax, honey and slaves from Kievan Rus' south to Byzantium.
